name: Enforce remediation timeframes with inventory-driven scope and governed risk acceptance
description: Drive scan scope from the authoritative asset inventory, put an SLA clock on every finding, and give overruns a formal, authorised, time-bounded risk acceptance path instead of leaving them open.

steps.action: Make the asset inventory authoritative for scan scope, and reconcile scanned assets against it after every scan.
Extend coverage to container images and third-party dependencies, not only hosts.
Auto-create a tracked work item per finding, carrying a due date derived from the policy timeframe for its severity.
Alert on approaching and breached due dates so overruns surface before period end rather than during fieldwork.
Implement a risk acceptance workflow requiring a named authoriser, a documented rationale, a compensating control, and a mandatory expiry date.
Verify remediation by rescan rather than by ticket closure.
Recalibrate the policy timeframes against what the organization actually achieves; unrealistic published timeframes manufacture exceptions.

implementation_considerations: Recalibrating published timeframes is politically harder than tightening tooling, but it is often the change that removes the exceptions.
Ephemeral infrastructure needs continuous discovery rather than scheduled scans; scheduled scanning alone will keep producing coverage gaps.
typical_duration: Weeks for tooling and workflow; one full cycle to demonstrate adherence.
prerequisites: A scanner able to cover the asset classes in the boundary

verification_method.how: For a completed period, confirm every scan reconciles to the inventory, every finding has a due date derived from its severity, and every overrun carries an authorised time-bounded risk acceptance.

residual_risk_note: Ephemeral and auto-scaled assets can appear and disappear between scans; inventory-driven scope reduces but does not eliminate blind spots without continuous discovery.
period_limitation_note: Remediating an overdue vulnerability now does not remove the overrun that occurred during an elapsed examination period.
notes: Step 7 is deliberate: DriftGuard should not recommend the shortest possible timeframes, because the organization is measured against whatever it publishes.
